key_insight: An invariant neural-network closure brings two-equation RANS-like turbulence behavior to coarse-mesh reactor simulations without solving turbulence transport equations.
engineering_relevance: The closure improves molten-salt reactor flow predictions at system-code cost, using about 0.2 core-hours versus 330 core-hours for the Nek5000 reference transient.
method: Predict elementwise turbulent kinetic energy and timescale from neighboring flow and geometry.
Enforce translation, Galilean, rotation, reflection, and neighbor-order invariance; place non-negative eddy viscosity in the implicit diffusive operator.
Iteratively retrain on SAM flow states against fixed Nek5000 targets to reduce solver-induced covariate shift.
evidence_signal: On a held-out steady state, the closure recovered the reference recirculation cell and eddy-viscosity plume; during a 120 s pump coastdown, velocity error fell from 37.6% to 17.7%, with 12% time-averaged eddy-viscosity error.
watch_item: Coarse-mesh resolution still limits velocity accuracy, and the abstract does not establish generalization beyond the evaluated MSFR conditions.
paper_title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics
